newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end lower after steady erosion.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end lower after steady erosion.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended sharply lower after prices steadily eroded into the last 30 minutes of pit trade, as the U.S. dollar corrected Tuesday's losses, traders and analysts said.
They said strength in the U.S. bond market, coupled with technical factors, led traders and dealers, who became short against the dollar Tuesday, to cover their positions.

"There was no reason for the (December) yen to rally as much as it did yesterday," one floor trader said about the contract's rally to $0.009270 after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided Tuesday not to raise U.S. rates.
December yen set a new contract low late in the day at $0.009151, through support at $0.009158 as dollar/yen rallied to 110.45 spot.

"The dollar is just returning to the levels they were trading at before the FOMC announcement yesterday," one cash forex source said. The dollar/yen fell to 108.95 spot in reaction to the FOMC's announcement that they were not tightening U.S. monetary policy.
Likewise, the dollar/mark retraced Tuesday's decline and rose above 1.5162 spot. December marks hit sell-stops at $0.6630, the futures equivalent of Tuesday's high of 1.5162.
Earlier, sell-stop orders were touched off at $0.6638.
"Dealers continued to offer the market, and locals just ran with it," a trader said, adding December marks could test $0.6619, or 1.5190 spot, in the near term.
"It's going to be a slow, steady grind up for the dollar," he said.
"People are re-considering the fundamentals," another floor trader said. "Even though the Fed did nothing, the interest rate differentials still favor the U.S."
Also, some cash dealers attributed dollar/mark's rally to the cash mark's poor performance against the Italian lira.
Cash mark/lira cross dipped below 1000 in late afternoon dealings in the U.S.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was down $0.000113 to $0.009154, marks fell $0.0067 to $0.6632, Swiss francs were off $0.0099 to $0.8128, Sterling was $0.0054 lower to $1.5602, Canadian dollar was down $0.0005 to $0.7342, Australian dollars were up $0.0045 at $0.7887, Mexican pesos were down $0.000075 to $0.126250 and the Brazilian real was up $0.00090 at $0.96900.
